findings.title: Verify the helper using the collector’s digest format
findings.trigger: Inventory a gate-autoreview-v2 receipt with its exact, unchanged helper and valid archived dataset.
findings.evidence: gate.mjs computes helperDigest with runtime.digest(helperText), which hashes canonical JSON, including string quoting and escapes. This comparison hashes raw file bytes instead. Consequently, authentic receipts are excluded as 'helper version unavailable' even with the correct helper. withCase repeats the incompatible verification. The fixtures manufacture raw-byte digests and therefore miss the producer/consumer mismatch.

findings.title: Reject repository symlinks before materializing datasets
findings.trigger: The pinned tree contains an .orchestrator symlink pointing to an existing directory outside the temporary checkout, such as evidenceRoot.
findings.evidence: Checkout preserves the symlink. Recursive mkdir accepts the existing directory target, and writeFileSync follows the symlink when creating review-dataset-<digest>.md. Thus even admission dry-runs can write outside scratch and into the archive. Unlike decisions.mjs materialization, this path never verifies that .orchestrator is a plain directory contained in the checkout.

findings.title: Disable lazy fetching during offline Git inspection
findings.trigger: The supplied repository is a partial clone with a missing blob needed by the pinned diff and a configured promisor remote.
findings.evidence: evidence() invokes Git diff with an environment that omits GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. Git can therefore fetch missing objects from the remote during manifest inventory or compatibility preparation. This violates the offline protocol and replaces the required unavailable-object exclusion with a network operation. The existing gate’s hardened Git environment explicitly disables lazy fetching.

findings.title: Make diff hashing independent of repository configuration
findings.trigger: The source repository has local diff.noprefix=true and a nonempty pinned change.
findings.evidence: The source diff respects local diff configuration, so its digest uses paths without a/ and b/. withCase initializes a fresh repository without that configuration and recomputes the digest with default prefixes. The identical commits and tree then fail 'copied code differs', excluding every otherwise compatible route. Binary and full-index flags do not normalize these settings.

findings.title: Validate malformed routes before traversing credentials
findings.trigger: A custom routes JSON contains credentialEnv as a string, or contains a null route alongside valid routes.
findings.evidence: CLI loading calls credentialValues before admission. It assumes every route is non-null and credentialEnv supports map, so malformed declarations abort the entire command instead of producing route exclusions. Direct admission also calls r.id and credentialEnv.some without safe schema guards. One malformed candidate therefore prevents valid candidates from being evaluated.

findings.title: Preflight the declared sample instead of every inventory case
findings.trigger: The manifest inventories two cases, the plan selects only one, and the unselected case fails helper preparation or requires objects no longer available.
findings.evidence: buildManifest retains the entire inventory, but admitRoutes loops over manifest.cases. A failure on the unselected case excludes the route before runBench reaches selectedCases. Consequently, removing an incompatible case from the declared experiment cannot make the remaining valid sample runnable.

findings.title: Account for provider calls inside multi-pass reviews
findings.trigger: A frozen case partitions into multiple helper review passes and maxCalls is one.
findings.evidence: The bench increments calls once and sets providerCalls=1 for the entire helper invocation. The helper can invoke the reviewer separately for each partition; the repository’s review ledger already distinguishes helper invocations from announced and confirmed passes. This invocation has no remaining-call constraint, so multiple provider calls can exceed maxCalls while the report records only one.

findings.title: Persist an attempt record before starting the paid call
findings.trigger: The bench process exits after invoking a provider but before that sample finishes.
findings.evidence: sampleId, case, protocol and providerCalls remain only in memory until this write after the helper returns. started.json contains only the manifest digest and run start time. An interrupted first call therefore leaves no individual attempt record, preventing the documented recovery procedure from identifying and counting its incomplete outcome.

findings.title: Terminate detached helper groups when the bench is interrupted
findings.trigger: The operator sends SIGINT or SIGTERM while a silent provider call is running on a POSIX system.
findings.evidence: The helper starts in a detached process group, and stop() is called only for timeout or output overflow. There is no parent cancellation handler. Terminating the bench therefore leaves the helper and reviewer running independently, allowing paid work to continue after the attempt has been abandoned and bypassing temporary-directory cleanup.

findings.title: Preserve source locations during anonymization
findings.trigger: A finding references src/anthropic.ts while the default Anthropic route is declared.
findings.evidence: Identity replacement operates on the serialized entire finding, including code_location. The provider identity 'anthropic' changes that path to src/[route].ts, which cannot locate the supplied source. Valid custom route IDs such as 'line' can also replace JSON field names. runBench stores only the altered finding, so the original grading evidence is lost.

findings.title: Require an actual fix member for each defect pair
findings.trigger: A plan contains a defect and a clean case from the same cluster, both carrying pair='pair-1', with no fix case.
findings.evidence: The lookup accepts any case whose kind differs from the current member, so the clean case satisfies the defect’s pair check. Clean cases are skipped by the outer validation loop. This plan freezes successfully and reportBench counts the pair despite there being no corresponding fix experiment.

findings.title: Report misses by family, risk, repeat and actual pair
findings.trigger: A route detects a defect in one family or repeat but misses it in another.
findings.evidence: Summaries group only by route, protocol and partition. casesByRisk lists inventory metadata without detection results, and pairedMisses merely sums all missed gold observations without consulting pair IDs or fix outcomes. Swapping which family, repeat or pair failed leaves the reported metrics unchanged, so the required breakdown and pair-level comparison cannot be inspected.

findings.title: Keep confirmed novel defects out of unresolved outcomes
findings.trigger: A completed sample has one finding adjudicated as novel, with reviewer evidence and no disputed or ungraded findings.
findings.evidence: scoreBench records the confirmed novel finding separately, but reportBench adds sum('novel') to unresolvedOutcomes. The fully adjudicated sample therefore reports an unresolved outcome. This contradicts the protocol’s distinction between confirmed novel defects and observations still awaiting adjudication.

findings.title: Calculate uncertainty by resampling whole families
findings.trigger: An experiment includes multiple families with several versions and repetitions per family.
findings.evidence: The report returns pooled detection ratios but no uncertainty estimate or family-resampling result. Correlated versions and repetitions enter the totals without any cluster-level analysis. The contract explicitly requires uncertainty estimated by resampling whole families; the interpretation string does not supply that analysis.

findings.title: Use the collector's helper digest algorithm
findings.trigger: Inventory a gate-produced receipt with its exact original helper bytes available.
findings.evidence: gate.mjs computes helperDigest using runtime.digest(fs.readFileSync(helper, 'utf8')), which hashes the canonical JSON string representation. This comparison hashes raw bytes instead, so even the original helper is excluded as 'helper version unavailable'. withCase repeats the raw-byte comparison. The new fixtures conceal this incompatibility by constructing receipts with raw SHA-256.

findings.title: Reject symlinked dataset parent directories
findings.trigger: An admitted archived commit contains a .orchestrator symlink to an existing directory outside the temporary checkout.
findings.evidence: Checkout preserves the symlink, recursive mkdir accepts its directory target, and writeFileSync follows the parent symlink when creating review-dataset-<digest>.md. No containment check precedes the write. Even admission during run --dry-run therefore writes outside scratch, potentially into the archive, and temporary-directory cleanup leaves that file behind.

findings.title: Account for provider calls inside partitioned reviews
findings.trigger: A frozen case requires multiple helper review passes and the remaining maxCalls budget is one.
findings.evidence: The pinned helper's supported partitioning invokes the reviewer separately for each pass; review-ledger.mjs already distinguishes internal passes using pass_reports. This runner reserves and records exactly one provider call for the entire helper invocation. A two-pass case can exceed maxCalls while run.calls and the report still claim one call, invalidating the declared budget and provider-call accounting.

findings.title: Normalize optional sidecar fields before sealing
findings.trigger: The helper produces report and status JSON, but the status sidecar omits reason; the result validator accepts this shape.
findings.evidence: helperStatus receives reason: undefined. runtime.canonical includes undefined-valued object properties when seal computes the run digest, whereas write's JSON.stringify omits them. Consequently the persisted run.json has a different canonical digest, and the score CLI rejects it on reload. Partial sidecars with other missing fields cause the same failure instead of remaining reportable operational failures.

findings.title: Require an actual fix as the defect's pair
findings.trigger: A plan contains a defect and a clean case in the same cluster, both with pair='pair-1', and contains no fix.
findings.evidence: Clean cases may carry a pair field, and the lookup accepts any different kind. The defect therefore finds the clean case, while the clean case is excluded from the validation loop. The invalid plan freezes successfully and reportBench counts the defect's pair toward pair coverage despite the required fix being absent.

findings.title: Validate route shapes before extracting credentials
findings.trigger: A custom routes array contains a valid route alongside a malformed route with credentialEnv='ZAI_API_KEY' instead of an array.
findings.evidence: buildManifest and the CLI call credentialValues before routeCheck. Calling .map on that string throws, aborting inventory or the whole experiment rather than recording a schema exclusion for the malformed route. routeCheck also later calls .some without confirming the field is an array, so guarding only credentialValues would not complete the fix.

findings.title: Limit frozen-run admission to selected cases
findings.trigger: A manifest inventories an unselected case whose helper dry-run fails, while every case selected by the plan passes for the route.
findings.evidence: Admission checks every inventoried case and excludes the entire route on the first failure. runBench subsequently schedules only selectedCases(manifest). Thus an incompatible input outside the declared experiment can prevent all selected samples from running, even though their exact compatibility checks would pass.

findings.title: Preserve source locations during anonymization
findings.trigger: A finding references a real path containing a default provider identity, such as providers/anthropic.py.
findings.evidence: Identity replacement runs over the entire serialized finding, including code_location. The default anthropic provider declaration turns that path into providers/[route].py. The altered location is persisted in both private samples and blind.json, leaving graders without the actual source location needed to verify the finding.

findings.title: Report outcomes by family, risk and repeat
findings.trigger: A run includes multiple families, risk classes or repetitions with different detection and failure outcomes.
findings.evidence: Summaries aggregate only by anonymous route, protocol and partition. casesByRisk lists case metadata without outcomes, and the report omits per-case matched gold and repeat results. Consequently report cannot show the contract's required misses by family, risk and repeat or identify which defect/fix pairs account for the aggregate misses.

findings.anchor: test('freeze recoverable inputs, deduplicate receipt/history, explain exclusions')
findings.title: Connect the bench fixtures to repository verification
findings.trigger: CI or a maintainer runs the documented node scripts/verify.mjs verification entry point.
findings.evidence: .github/workflows/validate.yml runs only verify.mjs. That script uses an explicit test-file list without review-bench.test.mjs, and validate-workflow.mjs does not invoke this suite either. None of the new bench behavior fixtures execute during normal verification, allowing regressions in the installed runner to go unchecked.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: inventory any gate-autoreview-v2 receipt with its exact helper. gate.mjs:386 stores helperDigest=digest(readFileSync(helper,'utf8')) and runtime.mjs:24 defines digest=sha256(canonical(value)), where canonical of a string is JSON.stringify (added quotes/escapes). review-bench.mjs:80 compares sha256 of raw bytes, so the comparison can never succeed and every authentic case is excluded as 'helper version unavailable'; withCase:191 repeats it. The delivered feasibility record (docs/review-bench-protocol.md: 'five had a versioned dataset but no available helper copy matching the receipt's digest') is therefore a wrong conclusion attributed to archive availability instead of a digest-format mismatch. Excluding other cases: no archive bytes are altered (data), no credential is exposed (security), nothing unverified is admitted (gate-bypass), and the readiness fact is present but misread, so the primary consequence is a silently wrong inventory/feasibility result that also stalls every experiment.
verdicts.reason: Verified in code: producer uses canonical-JSON digest, consumer hashes raw bytes; the two values differ for every helper file, so no real receipt can ever pass line 80.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: a pinned tree containing a symlink entry '.orchestrator' -> an existing directory outside the checkout (e.g. the evidence root). withCase:196 checks out that tree, :198 mkdirSync('.orchestrator',{recursive:true}) succeeds because stat follows the symlink to a directory, and :200 writeFileSync creates review-dataset-<digest>.md through the symlink, outside the temp scratch. No containment check exists on that path, and the finally rmSync of temp does not remove the external file. This happens even during run --dry-run admission, contradicting 'The bench never edits archive files' and 'Dry runs ... do not write to the archive': retained archive content is added to outside the reserved bench directory. Excluding others: no credentials are written there (security), no verification is skipped (gate-bypass/stall), the sample result itself stays correct (silent-result), and no readiness fact is dropped.
verdicts.reason: Code proof: no symlink/containment check between checkout (:196) and the dataset write (:200); recursive mkdir accepts a symlinked directory and writeFileSync follows the parent symlink.

verdicts.dangerReason: baseEnvironment (review-bench.mjs:20-24) sets GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM/GLOBAL, GIT_NO_REPLACE_OBJECTS and GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT but omits GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH, which gate.mjs:15 does set. On a blobless/partial clone with a promisor remote, evidence() line 51 'git diff --binary --full-index base head' needs missing blobs and git fetches them over the network during read-only inventory or admission preparation, instead of producing the contract's 'unavailable objects are excluded' exclusion. Missing evidence to rate the consequence: whether the promisor remote's URL and a repo-local credential helper would transmit credentials to that host (security) cannot be excluded without the operator's repo configuration; the diff digest itself stays correct after a successful fetch, so silent-result is not established either. Danger therefore remains uncertain rather than cleared.
verdicts.reason: Verified divergence from the existing hardened git environment; the offline protocol and the required unavailable-object exclusion can be replaced by a network fetch.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: source repository with local diff config (e.g. diff.noprefix=true, or diff.algorithm/diff.context) and a non-empty pinned change. GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM/GLOBAL suppress only system/global config, so evidence() at :51 computes the diff digest under the source repo's local settings, while withCase:194 creates a fresh 'git init' copy without them and recomputes it at :197. Identical commits and trees then fail 'copied code differs'; admitRoutes:225 turns this into 'compatibility input unavailable' and excludes every route, so a fully valid experiment can never run and the recorded reason misstates the cause. Excluding others: nothing is written outside the run directory (data), no credential involved (security), nothing unverified is admitted (gate-bypass), gold/recall numbers are never produced (silent-result), and the exclusion record is present (readiness).
verdicts.reason: Code proof: the same digest is computed in two repositories with different effective diff configuration and then compared for exact equality; --binary/--full-index do not normalize prefix, algorithm or context settings.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: a routes JSON containing one valid route plus a malformed one with credentialEnv:'ZAI_API_KEY' (or a null element). credentialValues (:31-33) does (route.credentialEnv??[]).map(...) and is called before any validation in buildManifest:56 and in the CLI at :382/:389, so .map on a string (or property access on null) throws and the entire manifest/run command aborts. routeCheck:154 also calls route?.credentialEnv?.some(...) unguarded, so admitRoutes throws as well. The contract requires schema errors to exclude that route; instead valid candidate routes are refused evaluation. Excluding others: the abort happens before any provider call so nothing unverified is admitted (gate-bypass) and no results are produced (silent-result); no files are written (data) and no credential is printed (security, the message is redacted at :400).
verdicts.reason: Verified: credential extraction and routeCheck both traverse credentialEnv without an array guard on the paths that run before admission, so one malformed declaration blocks the whole command instead of being recorded as an exclusion.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: manifest inventories two cases, the plan selects only one, and the unselected case fails the helper dry-run or its objects are unavailable. admitRoutes:221 iterates manifest.cases (the whole inventory, which buildManifest always retains) and breaks the route out on the first failure, while runBench:253 schedules only selectedCases(manifest). There is no option to narrow the inventory, so an input outside the declared experiment permanently refuses every selected sample whose own compatibility check would pass. Excluding others: no writes outside the run dir (data), no credential handling (security), nothing unverified is admitted (gate-bypass), no numbers are emitted (silent-result), and the exclusion reason is recorded (readiness).
verdicts.reason: Code proof: admission loops over manifest.cases while the run uses selectedCases; contract binds admission to the frozen cases of the declared sample.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: a frozen case the pinned helper partitions into several review passes with maxCalls nearly exhausted. runBench:271 increments calls once and sets providerCalls=1 per helper invocation, and the invocation carries no remaining-call constraint. The helper announces 'review passes: N' (gate.mjs:140) and reports pass_reports per pass (review-ledger.mjs:51), i.e. N separate reviewer calls; wave-cost.mjs:372 sums those passes. So real provider calls exceed the predeclared maxCalls while run.calls, summaries.called and the usage coverage denominator (:358) all report one call per sample, making the reported cost/availability comparison and the budget stop rule wrong. Excluding others: artifacts are still written (data), credentials remain redacted (security), the declared gold scoring is unaffected (gate-bypass/stall), and the usage counters themselves are summed correctly by parseReviewUsage (readiness).
verdicts.reason: Verified against the helper's own multi-pass representation in this repository; one invocation can consume several reviewer calls that the bench neither counts nor bounds.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: the bench is interrupted after the paid invoke at :272 and before the write at :293. started.json (:248) holds only manifestDigest and startedAt, and sampleId/caseId/protocol/providerCalls exist only in memory until the post-call write, so the in-flight attempt leaves no sample-*.json. The contract's recovery procedure ('After interruption inspect started.json and individual sample-*.json files; count that attempted experiment and its incomplete outcomes'; 'Never drop an interrupted attempt when comparing cost or availability') then cannot count that paid call, so cost/availability comparisons silently omit it. Excluding others: existing files are not modified (data corruption), no credential is exposed (security), no verification is skipped for admitted work (gate-bypass), and nothing legitimate is refused (gate-stall).
verdicts.reason: Code proof: the durable per-sample record is written only after the helper returns; no attempt record is reserved before the call.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: SIGINT/SIGTERM on POSIX during a live call. invoke:176 spawns the helper detached (its own process group, so it does not receive the terminal's SIGINT) and stop() at :177 is wired only to the timeout and overflow paths; there is no parent cancellation handler. The parent dies, the helper and its reviewer keep running and billing, the finally rmSync at :203 never executes so the scratch copy of helper/dataset persists, and no sample record or run.json is written for that attempt, so the abandoned paid call is invisible to the study log and to cost/availability comparison. Excluding others: archive files are untouched (data), only temp files remain; nothing unverified is admitted (gate-bypass) and no valid work is refused (gate-stall).
verdicts.reason: Verified: detached child with kill logic only on timeout/overflow and no SIGINT/SIGTERM handling, so interruption orphans the reviewer and loses the attempt record.

verdicts.dangerReason: Concrete path: a returned finding whose code_location is e.g. providers/anthropic.py or src/anthropic.ts while the default routes are declared (provider ids anthropic, zai, moonshot, deepseek, xai, minimax, google, openai; route ids incumbent, glm, kimi, grok, gemini...). blindFinding:237-239 serializes the whole finding, including code_location, and replaces every identity case-insensitively with '[route]', producing providers/[route].py. runBench:284 stores only that altered finding in both sample-*.json and blind.json, so the grader and the private record lose the actual source location needed to adjudicate; a route id matching a JSON key would also rename fields. Altering retained evidence is data even though '[route]' is a recognizable marker. Excluding others: no credential is leaked (security, redact still runs), gold matching still requires evidence (gate-bypass), nothing is refused (gate-stall), and the sample status/usage stay correct (silent-result).
verdicts.reason: Code proof: identity substitution runs over the serialized object rather than over free-text fields, and no unaltered copy of the finding is retained anywhere.

findings.title: Use the archive producer's helper digest algorithm
findings.trigger: Inventory a genuine gate receipt with its exact historical helper available, including through --helper.
findings.evidence: gate.mjs computes helperDigest with runtime.digest(fs.readFileSync(helper, 'utf8')); runtime.digest hashes canonical JSON, including string quoting and escaping. This comparison instead hashes raw bytes, so an unchanged helper is rejected as unavailable. withCase repeats the incompatible check. The new fixtures manufacture raw-byte digests and therefore miss this incompatibility.

findings.title: Reject symlinked dataset parent directories
findings.trigger: A frozen commit tracks .orchestrator as a symlink to an existing directory outside the temporary repository, such as the archive's datasets directory.
findings.evidence: Checkout recreates the symlink. mkdirSync with recursive:true and the subsequent writeFileSync follow that directory symlink, creating review-dataset-<digest>.md outside the temporary repository. Neither evidence nor withCase checks this parent. Even run --dry-run can consequently write into the archive, and temporary-directory cleanup leaves the external file behind.

findings.title: Redact credentials before anonymizing route names
findings.trigger: A credential contains a route identity, for example a key beginning xai- with provider.id xai, and the helper includes that key in a finding body.
findings.evidence: blindFinding replaces xai with [route] before credential redaction runs. The transformed string no longer matches the original credential or its base64 form, so the remaining credential material is persisted in sample files, run.json and blind.json. Replacing the known route prefix reconstructs the original key. Later write-time redaction cannot recognize the transformed value either.

findings.title: Keep finding structure and source locations intact
findings.trigger: A finding points to src/glm/parser.js while the default glm route is declared, or a custom route has an allowed ID such as body.
findings.evidence: Route replacement runs across serialized JSON, including code_location and property names. The default glm identity changes the real source path to src/[route]/parser.js; a route named body renames the body property itself. The damaged finding is then saved as the grading evidence, preventing graders from reliably locating or reading the observation.

findings.title: Account for every reviewer pass in the call limit
findings.trigger: A large frozen input requires two helper review passes and the plan declares maxCalls: 1.
findings.evidence: The helper protocol supports partitioning one review into multiple reviewer passes, but the bench increments calls once per helper process and always records providerCalls as one. It neither reserves the dry-run pass count nor limits the helper's pass budget. One allowed invocation can therefore exceed the declared provider-call limit, while run.calls and report usage denominators undercount the calls.

findings.title: Disable lazy fetching during archive inspection
findings.trigger: The supplied repository is a partial clone with a locally available commit but missing promised trees or blobs.
findings.evidence: evidence invokes ls-tree and diff using the repository's local configuration without GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. Git can contact the promisor remote and write downloaded objects into the source repository instead of excluding unavailable inputs. This breaks the offline, read-only inventory contract. The existing gate's safeGitEnv explicitly disables lazy fetching.

findings.title: Validate route shapes before collecting credential names
findings.trigger: A custom routes array contains a valid route and a malformed route whose credentialEnv is a string, or contains null.
findings.evidence: Both CLI loading and buildManifest call credentialValues before routeCheck. Accessing a null route or calling .map on a string throws and aborts the entire command, so the valid route is never evaluated. Other malformed shapes also reach unchecked .some calls in routeCheck. The contract requires schema errors to exclude the affected route, not terminate the experiment.

findings.title: Preflight the declared sample instead of the whole inventory
findings.trigger: The plan selects compatible cases, while another reproducible but unselected inventory case has a pinned helper or input that fails the candidate's dry-run.
findings.evidence: buildManifest retains every inventoried case regardless of plan selection. admitRoutes checks every manifest.cases entry and excludes the route after any failure, whereas runBench later executes only selectedCases(manifest). An unrelated case outside the declared experiment can therefore prevent all valid selected samples from running.

findings.title: Require an actual fix in every defect pair
findings.trigger: A plan gives a defect and a clean case in the same cluster the same pair ID, with no fix case.
findings.evidence: The counterpart search accepts any different kind, including clean. Clean cases may carry pair because their pair field is not rejected. Consequently this plan passes pair validation, and reportBench counts the defect’s pair toward coverage despite there being no independently inspected corresponding fix. The validation must distinguish defect/fix counterparts explicitly.

findings.title: Calculate paired misses from aligned results
findings.trigger: The incumbent detects defect A and misses B, while a candidate misses A and detects B on the same declared cases and repeats.
findings.evidence: pairedMisses merely sums total minus detected independently for each route. Both routes receive the same value despite the candidate losing a defect the incumbent detected. The calculation never uses selection.pair, gold identities across routes, or aligned repeats, so the required pair-level regression evidence is absent.

findings.title: Report misses by family, risk class and repeat
findings.trigger: A run contains multiple task families or repeats whose detection results differ.
findings.evidence: The report aggregates scores only by anonymous route, protocol and partition. casesByRisk lists case metadata without detection results, and the per-sample usage entries contain no scores or case identities. Consequently report.json cannot show the contract-required counts and misses by family, risk class and repeat, hiding concentrated failures and repeat instability.

findings.title: Match the receipt producer’s helper digest algorithm
findings.trigger: Inventory a receipt produced by gate.mjs with an exact, unchanged copy of its helper.
findings.evidence: gate.mjs computes helperDigest with runtime.digest(fs.readFileSync(helper,'utf8')); runtime.digest hashes canonical(value), which JSON-encodes strings. The bench instead hashes raw helper bytes. Thus even the exact historical helper fails this comparison and the case is excluded. withCase repeats the incompatible comparison. The fixtures conceal the integration failure by constructing receipts with raw-byte hashes.

findings.title: Reject symlinked dataset directories before writing
findings.trigger: An archived head contains a tracked .orchestrator symlink pointing to an existing directory outside the temporary checkout, such as the archive’s datasets directory.
findings.evidence: Checkout preserves the symlink, recursive mkdir accepts its directory target, and writeFileSync follows it when creating review-dataset-<digest>.md. flag:'wx' prevents replacement of an existing leaf but does not prevent traversal through the parent symlink. Admission, including run --dry-run, consequently writes outside scratch; temporary-directory cleanup leaves that external file behind.

findings.title: Disable lazy fetching during archive inspection
findings.trigger: The supplied repository is a partial clone with available commits and trees but a missing promisor blob needed by the pinned diff.
findings.evidence: evidence() invokes git diff against the original repository, but baseEnvironment does not set GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. Git can fetch the missing blob from its configured promisor remote and write it into the original object database during manifest --dry-run. This contacts the network and mutates the inspected repository instead of excluding unavailable objects. The existing gate.mjs hardened environment explicitly disables lazy fetching.

findings.title: Account for every internal reviewer call
findings.trigger: A frozen case exceeds the helper’s prompt budget and requires multiple review passes while maxCalls has room for only one additional provider request.
findings.evidence: The runner reserves and reports exactly one call per helper invocation regardless of its internal passes. The repository already distinguishes helper invocations from internal-pass events and reads report.pass_reports in review-ledger.mjs. A two-pass invocation can therefore make two reviewer requests with maxCalls:1 while run.calls and sample.providerCalls both report one. Usage coverage denominators are understated as well.

findings.anchor: runBench: durable sample write after invocation
findings.title: Persist attempted samples before launching providers
findings.trigger: The bench process is interrupted after a paid invocation starts but before it finishes and reaches the sample-file write.
findings.evidence: The sample identity, case, repeat, protocol and providerCalls counter exist only in memory until this write. started.json contains only a manifest digest and timestamp, and run.json is written after the entire experiment. Inspecting the documented recovery artifacts cannot distinguish a paid interrupted call from interruption during preparation, so attempted calls and incomplete outcomes cannot be retained accurately.

findings.title: Terminate detached helpers when the bench stops
findings.trigger: On Unix, the operator presses Ctrl-C or sends SIGTERM while a helper is running.
findings.evidence: The helper starts in a separate process group, so the foreground bench’s interrupt does not reach it. No signal handler invokes stop(); that function is used only by the timeout and output-limit callbacks. Once the bench exits, its timeout timer also disappears, allowing the helper and reviewer work to continue beyond the declared deadline.

findings.anchor: blindFinding: replace identities in serialized JSON
findings.title: Blind text without modifying JSON structure
findings.trigger: A valid custom route has a short ID such as 'n', and the helper returns a finding without code_location.
findings.evidence: Route identities are replaced throughout serialized JSON, including keys and JSON literals. For ID 'n', code_location:null becomes code_locatio[route]:[route]ull inside the serialized representation, making JSON.parse fail. runBench then marks the successful review as failed and discards its findings. With populated locations, the same replacement corrupts field names such as line_range and end.

findings.anchor: runBench: production route differs from archived route
findings.title: Exclude incompatible cases from the production experiment
findings.trigger: The selected sample contains both medium- and high-effort archived cases, while the declared baseline uses high effort.
findings.evidence: Production samples are created for every case before route matching; incompatible cases become not-run samples. scoreBench nevertheless assigns their full gold denominator, and reportBench includes them as misses in production recall. A baseline that detects every eligible defect can therefore receive reduced recall solely because unrelated archived routes were never eligible for this experiment.

findings.title: Validate routes before collecting credential names

findings.title: Use the collector's helper digest algorithm
findings.trigger: Inventory a receipt produced by gate.mjs with its exact, unchanged helper available.
findings.evidence: gate.mjs computes helperDigest with runtime.digest(fs.readFileSync(helper, 'utf8')); runtime.digest hashes the canonical JSON representation of that string. This comparison instead hashes raw file bytes, so the unchanged helper is excluded as 'helper version unavailable'. withCase repeats the raw-byte comparison. The scratch fixtures manufacture raw-byte receipt digests and therefore miss the incompatibility with actual collector receipts.

findings.title: Reject dataset directories that escape the temporary repository
findings.trigger: A pinned tree contains an .orchestrator symlink pointing to an existing directory outside the temporary repository, including the evidence archive.
findings.evidence: Checkout preserves the symlink. Recursive mkdir and the subsequent dataset write follow it, creating review-dataset-<digest>.md outside scratch even during admission dry-run. No containment or symlink check protects this path, and temporary-repository cleanup leaves the external file behind.

findings.title: Disable lazy fetching during archive inspection
findings.trigger: The supplied repository is a partial clone whose pinned diff references a missing promisor blob.
findings.evidence: evidence() invokes git diff without GIT_NO_LAZY_FETCH. Git can fetch the missing blob from the configured promisor remote and update the source object store during manifest --dry-run. Missing objects should instead be excluded under the offline, read-only inventory contract. The existing gate's safeGitEnv explicitly disables lazy fetching.

findings.title: Validate route shapes before extracting credentials
findings.trigger: A custom routes array contains credentialEnv as a string, alongside otherwise valid routes.
findings.evidence: credentialValues calls .map on that string before routeCheck can record an exclusion. Manifest construction and the CLI abort instead of excluding the malformed route. Direct admission also reaches credentialEnv.some despite its earlier failed array check, aborting the remaining routes.

findings.title: Restrict anonymization to finding prose
findings.trigger: An accepted custom route has id 'body', or a finding's source path contains a default provider name such as google.
findings.evidence: Replacement operates on the entire serialized finding. Route id 'body' renames the body property to '[route]'; provider 'google' rewrites code_location paths containing that substring. Both private samples and blind.json retain only these altered findings, losing the original schema or usable source location needed for grading.

findings.title: Accept the helper's supported clean status
findings.trigger: An admitted historical helper returns a valid schema-version-1 sidecar with status 'clean', exit code zero and an empty findings array.
findings.evidence: The collector explicitly accepts 'clean', 'scoped-clean' and 'filtered', but this allowlist omits 'clean'. The successful call becomes 'failed' with 'missing or invalid helper result'. reportBench also omits 'clean' from completed results, inflating operational failures for supported helper versions.

findings.title: Require the opposite defect/fix member
findings.trigger: A plan contains a defect and a clean case from one cluster sharing a pair ID, with no fix case.
findings.evidence: Clean cases may carry pair IDs, and the counterpart search accepts any different kind. The clean case satisfies the defect's counterpart check and is itself skipped by the validation loop. reportBench then counts the pair toward coverage despite the missing corresponding fix.

findings.title: Count confirmed novel defects as adjudicated findings
findings.trigger: A completed sample has one confirmed novel defect and one adjudicated false positive.
findings.evidence: scoreBench records the confirmed defect under novel, but reportBench adds novel to unresolvedOutcomes and excludes it from the precision numerator and denominator. This produces precision zero and one unresolved finding instead of precision one-half and no unresolved findings. Novel defects must remain separate from gold recall without becoming unadjudicated observations.

findings.title: Preserve family, risk and repeat results in reports
findings.trigger: Selected families or repetitions have different detection results within the same partition.
findings.evidence: Summaries aggregate only by route, protocol and partition. casesByRisk contains case metadata without outcomes; pairedMisses is merely the aggregate missed-gold count. The report consequently omits the required family/risk/repeat miss breakdowns, pair-level results and family-resampled uncertainty, hiding whether failures concentrate in one family or recur across independent families.

findings.anchor: test('freeze recoverable inputs, deduplicate receipt/history, explain exclusions'
findings.title: Register the bench fixtures in repository verification
findings.trigger: A developer or CI runs the documented node scripts/verify.mjs entry point.
findings.evidence: verify.mjs enumerates test files explicitly and does not include review-bench.test.mjs. validate-workflow.mjs never invokes it either, and CI invokes only verify.mjs. The new behavioral suite therefore receives no execution through the repository's standard verification path.

findings.title: Reject symlinks before materializing the dataset
findings.trigger: A pinned repository contains a tracked .orchestrator symlink pointing to an existing writable directory outside the temporary repository.
findings.evidence: Checkout recreates the symlink, and mkdirSync plus writeFileSync follow it. The bench then creates review-dataset-<digest>.md outside its temporary directory, including during route admission dry runs. Removing temp only removes the symlink, leaving the external file behind. No real-path or directory-type check confines this write.

findings.title: Persist the sample before starting its provider call
findings.trigger: The bench process is interrupted while a live helper invocation is running.
findings.evidence: The call counter and active sample exist only in memory until invoke returns; sample-*.json is written at line 293 and run.json after every sample finishes. An interruption during the first paid invocation leaves started.json and route mappings without any record identifying the attempted case, repeat or call. The documented recovery artifacts therefore lose the very interrupted call that must remain in operational accounting.

findings.title: Normalize optional status fields before sealing
findings.trigger: A helper returns an otherwise accepted status sidecar without a reason property.
findings.evidence: The completed check does not require reason, and existing delivery-runtime fixtures use sidecars without it. This assignment creates reason: undefined. canonical includes that object key when sealing run, but JSON.stringify drops it when writing run.json. The subsequent CLI score command reads different content and fails verifySeal with 'frozen artifact digest mismatch'.

findings.title: Anonymize finding prose without changing its structure
findings.trigger: An admitted custom route has id 'body', or a finding references a source path such as src/gemini.ts with the default routes.
findings.evidence: Replacement runs over the entire serialized finding, including property names and code_location. The route id 'body' renames the body property to '[route]', while the default Gemini identity changes the actual source filename. These corrupted findings are saved in both private samples and blind.json, leaving graders without the original explanation or a usable source location.

findings.title: Check admission against the declared sample
findings.trigger: The inventory contains an unselected case whose pinned helper cannot prepare a candidate route, while every case selected by the plan supports it.
findings.evidence: buildManifest retains the whole inventory, but admission checks every manifest case and excludes the entire route on the first failure. runBench later executes only selectedCases(manifest). An unrelated case omitted from the experiment can therefore prevent all calls on a compatible declared sample.

findings.title: Require the opposite defect/fix kind in each pair
findings.trigger: A plan contains a defect and a clean case from one cluster with the same pair value, but no fix case.
findings.evidence: Clean cases may carry pair values, and the counterpart predicate accepts any different kind. The clean case satisfies this check for the defect, so the manifest freezes without a corresponding fix. reportBench then counts the defect's pair toward pair coverage despite the missing fix experiment.

findings.title: Validate route types before extracting credentials
findings.trigger: A custom routes array contains valid routes alongside a route with credentialEnv set to a string instead of an array.
findings.evidence: The CLI calls credentialValues before route admission, and this expression throws because the string has no map method. Direct admitRoutes calls also reach an unconditional credentialEnv.some after recording the schema error. Consequently one malformed route aborts the whole operation instead of being excluded with a reason while valid routes continue.

findings.title: Report outcomes by family, risk class and repeat
findings.trigger: A scored experiment contains multiple families, risk classes or repetitions with different detection outcomes.
findings.evidence: Result summaries group only by anonymous route, protocol and partition. casesByRisk lists input descriptors without scores, and the remaining per-sample entries contain only usage. The report therefore cannot identify family-specific misses, repeat instability or defect/fix pair outcomes, although the protocol explicitly requires those breakdowns.

findings.title: Calculate uncertainty using whole-family resampling
findings.trigger: A completed comparison contains several versions or repetitions per family and differing results across families.
findings.evidence: The report sums detected and total observations and returns point estimates only. It never groups observations for resampling or emits uncertainty estimates or an explanation that they are unavailable. Thus the contract's required family-level uncertainty analysis is absent, regardless of sample size.

verdicts.dangerReason: scripts/gate.mjs:386 writes helperDigest = digest(fs.readFileSync(helper,'utf8')), and runtime.mjs:24 defines digest as sha256(canonical(value)) = sha256(JSON.stringify(string)). review-bench.mjs:80 compares sha256 of the raw file bytes, which can never equal that value. Every receipt produced by the real collector is therefore excluded with reason 'helper version unavailable' even when the exact unchanged helper is present, and the same raw-byte comparison repeats at line 191. The result is a wrong inventory/feasibility conclusion: cases are reported as irreproducible for a fabricated reason, and the delivered feasibility record in docs/review-bench-protocol.md ('five had a versioned dataset but no available helper copy matching the receipt's digest') is produced by this mismatch rather than by actual input unavailability. data: archive files are only read; security: no credential path; gate-bypass: the bench issues no certificate; gate-stall: the refusal is of the bench's own sample construction, but its stated cause is false, which is a wrong result rather than a refusal of separate work; readiness: covered by the wrong reported cause.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. The collector hashes the canonical JSON form of the helper text; the bench hashes raw bytes, so no genuine collector receipt can ever match and the inventory/feasibility report attributes exclusions to a non-existent helper change. The scratch fixtures (review-bench.test.mjs:24) manufacture raw-byte digests and so never exercise a real receipt.

Minor, since the resulting digests remain correct and the offline case fails closed with an exclusion reason.

A route id 'body' (accepted by id() and by routeCheck) renames the body property to '[route]', and default provider identities such as 'google' or 'anthropic' rewrite matching substrings inside source paths. verdicts.reason: Confirmed in part: counting adjudicated novel findings in unresolvedOutcomes publishes a wrong unresolved figure. The reviewer's precision expectation is not established by the contract, which only requires precision with its adjudicated denominator; that part is not a defect. Minor because the error biases against candidates and the default outcome is unchanged.

findings.title: Reject executable Git filters before provisioning the worktree
findings.trigger: The repository config defines a smudge/process filter used by a tracked .gitattributes entry, and the Issue worktree does not exist.

findings.title: Reject executable Git filters before creating the worktree
findings.trigger: The repository config defines a smudge/process filter selected by a tracked .gitattributes entry, and the Issue worktree does not exist yet.
findings.evidence: prepareDispatch runs git worktree add before invoking gate.mjs start. Its Git wrapper disables hooks and fsmonitor but neither rejects executable filters nor isolates Git configuration. Checkout therefore executes the filter with orchestrator privileges before the existing rejectExecutableFilters check in gate.mjs can refuse the repository. This crosses the contract's privileged Git boundary.

findings.title: Register the resumed worker before consuming a resume-mode ack
findings.trigger: A dispatch uses the default handshake=resume, the worker acknowledges and exits, and the orchestrator submits the documented plan-bound read-backs.
findings.evidence: acceptAck passes the read-backs directly to consumeAck without preparing or invoking resume.mjs. consumeAck requires entry.last_resume to identify the newly registered writer and bind this ack's digest, so the documented flow ends with 'resumed writer registration for this ack required before consumption'. The lifecycle changes have already been performed, but the worker remains stopped. The fixture bypasses this integration by manually inserting last_resume.

findings.title: Allow invalid gate evidence to reach terminal rejection
findings.trigger: The orchestrator calls accept ack --outcome rejected for an ack with missing, foreign, duplicated, or malformed gates.
findings.evidence: validatedAck unconditionally enforces gate coverage and requires either passed or blocked before considering the rejected outcome. Consequently, precisely the artifacts that require rejection throw before consumeAck can journal rejection, rename the ack, and remove gates. The underlying consumer explicitly permits rejected artifacts without those validations. Recovery of a previously journaled rejection is blocked by the same checks.

findings.title: Validate every registry gate name before exposing a move plan
findings.trigger: A malformed registry contains gates=[17], and the ack contains one gate with gate=17, status=pass, and nonempty evidence.
findings.evidence: The registry validation checks only array presence, length, and uniqueness. Numeric names satisfy includes and the passed calculation, allowing acceptAck to print lifecycle instructions. consumeAck subsequently rejects the same registry because it requires nonempty string names. Connector mutations can therefore occur before the producer-contract error is detected, contrary to the required complete gate-list validation before lifecycle application.

findings.title: Apply attempt freshness and tombstone rules before planning
findings.trigger: Polling finds an otherwise valid named ack whose mtime predates the current attempt log, or finds an ack alongside an attempt tombstone without a trusted consumption record.
findings.evidence: validatedAck checks the registry log's basename, candidate count, and future timestamps, but never compares ack mtime with log birthtime or checks applied/rejected/blocked tombstones in either location. It can expose a new move plan for evidence that the watcher's readGateAck and ackBelongsToAttempt deliberately reject. The polling command can thus authorize lifecycle changes from stale or already-suppressed evidence.

findings.title: Check conflicts across the entire queue before printing writes
findings.trigger: A new report queues a new first write and then reuses an already recorded write ID with a changed payload.
findings.evidence: validateReportBarriers calls confirmQueue with an adapter that throws on the first write. confirmQueue checks each durable write digest immediately before its adapter call, so later writes are never checked during this validation. acceptReport then opens a session and prints the conflicting write for connector execution. Only final confirmation discovers the conflict, after the orchestrator may already have performed the forbidden mutation.

findings.title: Fence resume against the registered amendment version
findings.trigger: Two amendment commands overlap for the same stopped attempt: one registers version 1, the other registers version 2 before the first command's resume subprocess acquires launch.lock.
findings.evidence: Preparation releases launch.lock before invoking resume.mjs. The generated resume request contains neither the amendment version nor a value that resumeWorker compares with last_amendment. The first command can therefore launch its version-1 prompt while workers.json advertises version 2; the other resume then refuses the live process. Subsequent collection requests from that worker are rejected as stale, and the registered amendment has not reached the running worker.

findings.title: Preserve literal double braces inside snapshot content
findings.trigger: An approved Issue or document contains literal template syntax such as {{ user.name }} in a code example.
findings.evidence: Named substitutions insert the document bytes correctly, but the final regex scans the entire rendered result and treats the inserted literal as an unresolved generator placeholder. Dispatch refuses with 'unfilled dispatch placeholders remain' even though every placeholder in the dispatch template was filled. Valid work involving common template syntaxes cannot be launched without changing the approved snapshot.

findings.title: Retain coverage IDs after punctuation inside descriptive slugs
findings.trigger: A selected definition contains 'Покрывает R1 (API v1.0), R2.', and R2 is not independently selected.
findings.evidence: The coverage regex stops at every period, including the period inside v1.0. references receives only the fragment through 'API v1', so transitive selection includes R1 but silently omits R2. Since PRD requirements are not always-included common sections, the worker receives a short snapshot missing a requirement explicitly covered by its selected implementation unit.

findings.title: Respect the opening Markdown fence length
findings.trigger: A Spec uses a four-backtick fence to show a Markdown example containing triple-backtick fences and an example heading such as '## Кратко'.
findings.evidence: scan stores only the delimiter character and closes a fence on any following delimiter of that character. The inner triple-backtick line therefore closes the outer four-backtick fence prematurely, exposing example headings and IDs as real document structure. With the example Кратко heading, section reports a duplicate and refuses an otherwise valid short dispatch.

findings.title: Render the configured worker audience's required content
findings.trigger: A project uses the default gpt-worker audience, or switches orchestration.workerAudience between its supported values.
findings.evidence: prepareDispatch never reads workerAudience, and renderDispatch removes the generator instructions without implementing their audience-dependent expansion. The resulting prompt still tells the worker to 'Generate profile-required redundancy' and contains no generated parked-reason decision list or worked report/certificate shapes required for gpt-worker. Both configurations receive the same policy body, so the documented audience adapter is silently ignored.

findings.title: Reject executable Git filters before creating the worktree
findings.trigger: The product repository configures a smudge/process filter, origin/main contains a matching .gitattributes entry, and the dispatch worktree does not exist.
findings.evidence: git worktree add checks out files and can execute that filter on the orchestrator host. The new git wrapper disables hooks and fsmonitor but does not inspect filters. The rejecting startGate runs only after worktree creation, so its existing rejectExecutableFilters protection arrives after execution.

findings.title: Emit a gate-compatible representation for an absent dataset
findings.trigger: No review dataset is configured, and a preflight request copies the emitted Preflight pins, as the new test's request builder does.
findings.evidence: Dispatch explicitly emits reviewDataset:null, and acceptAmend preserves that representation. scripts/gate.mjs reviewDatasetBinding treats only undefined as absence; null enters the path-validation branch and is rejected. Consequently the default emitted pins cannot be copied directly into the collection or worker verification request.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Project-first seam contract
findings.trigger: A normal Project-first dispatch has no issue-only.json.
findings.evidence: The generated seam sets risk_class to the delivery risk and approval_status to approved/pending/rejected. scripts/resolve-issue-context.mjs projectFirstResult and references/issue-only-lane.md define the Project-first values as risk_class:null and approval_status:absent. Every such dispatch therefore supplies a purported resolved seam that contradicts the worker's required resolver; package approval must remain separate from these seam fields.

findings.title: Serialize structured issue-only facts before rendering
findings.trigger: issue-only.json supplies config and ownerApproval as JSON objects containing the configured owner and authenticated approval facts.
findings.evidence: These objects pass the truthiness checks and are assigned directly to template values. renderDispatch converts each with String(value), producing [object Object]. The worker's snapshot consequently loses the owner identity and approved fingerprint needed to resolve the issue-only seam, despite the command accepting and launching this input.

findings.title: Allow rejected consumption of invalid gate evidence
findings.trigger: The orchestrator calls ack --outcome rejected for a gates-passed ack missing a required gate, or retries consumption of the resulting rejected record.
findings.evidence: validatedAck requires passed or blocked even when outcome is rejected, and earlier checks reject malformed gate coverage unconditionally. The request never reaches consumeAck, whose rejected branch deliberately permits invalid gate evidence. This prevents the documented terminal rejection and its crash recovery, leaving the ack and registry gates unconsumed.

findings.title: Check that the acknowledgement belongs to the attempt log
findings.trigger: A well-shaped current-attempt ack filename already exists before that attempt's log is created, for example because an earlier worker precreated it in the shared writable mailbox.
findings.evidence: The command checks only the log basename and the ack's future timestamp; it never compares ack mtime with log birthtime. It therefore prints lifecycle instructions from evidence that predates this attempt. The watcher explicitly requires that lower timestamp bound, so polling through accept accepts an artifact the watcher would not deliver.

findings.title: Honor attempt tombstones before exposing a lifecycle plan
findings.trigger: One raw ack exists while an applied/rejected/blocked tombstone exists in the other delivery location, and there is no trusted private consumption record.
findings.evidence: validatedAck examines only the two raw .json paths and the private record. It never examines tombstones, so it treats the raw file as a new ack and prints a move plan. The contract and watcher's readGateAck suppress the entire attempt when either location contains a tombstone; the polling command bypasses that suppression.

findings.title: Register the resumed writer on the default handshake path
findings.trigger: Dispatch uses the default handshake=resume, the worker exits after its passed ack, and the orchestrator supplies fresh plan-bound lifecycle readbacks.
findings.evidence: acceptAck immediately calls consumeAck without preparing or invoking resume.mjs. consumeAck requires a matching last_resume writer registration for this path and refuses the ordinary gate-phase registry entry. Thus the documented plan → connector → readback command flow cannot complete for the default transport mode without a separate, undocumented resume operation.

findings.title: Validate every write before printing connector instructions
findings.trigger: A report contains two writes; the first is valid, while the second reuses a previously journaled write ID with a changed payload.
findings.evidence: confirmQueue checks each write's durable digest immediately before its adapter call. The sentinel throws on the first adapter call, so validation never reaches the second write. acceptReport then opens a session and prints both instructions. The orchestrator can apply the conflicting second payload before final confirmation finally rejects it, leaving an external mutation that cannot be confirmed.

findings.title: Check resume eligibility before activating an amendment
findings.trigger: accept amend is called while the registered worker process is still alive.
findings.evidence: The command publishes pins.vN.json and advances workers.json pinsVersion before calling resume.mjs. resumeWorker then refuses the live process, but the version change remains active. The existing worker continues with its previous dispatch and its next collection request is rejected as using stale pinsVersion, even though the amendment command failed and never delivered the new requirements.

verdicts.dangerReason: security: dispatch.mjs:83 runs `git worktree add` (a checkout) with the orchestrator's own privileges and its wrapper (dispatch.mjs:13) only sets core.fsmonitor=false and core.hooksPath=/dev/null. A repository-configured filter.<name>.smudge/process selected by a tracked .gitattributes entry is executed by that checkout on the orchestrator host, outside any worker sandbox. The only refusal exists in gate.mjs:34-39 via the git wrapper at gate.mjs:55, and gate start is invoked afterwards at dispatch.mjs:132, so the contract's 'the gate refuses before execution' boundary is crossed; no other check in the new path inspects filter config.

Breaking input: a product repo whose config defines filter.x.process/smudge with a matching .gitattributes entry in origin/main and no existing .worktrees/KEY. dispatch.mjs:81-83 fetches and creates the worktree (checkout applies smudge/process filters) before run("../gate.mjs", ["start"]) at line 132, which is the only place rejectExecutableFilters (gate.mjs:34) runs. The dispatch git wrapper disables hooks/fsmonitor but never inspects filters and does not isolate Git config. Privileged filter execution therefore precedes the fail-closed refusal the contract requires.

On refusal the plan file, the ack and registryEntry.gates all remain in place (nothing is renamed or removed before consumeAck succeeds), so no gate is bypassed, no durable evidence is altered, no readiness fact is lost, and the operation is retryable, so ordinary work is not permanently refused.

The orchestrator performs the resume with installed resume.mjs, which writes last_resume {pid, thread_id, gateAckDigest} (launch.mjs:116-117) from the still-present ack while gates are retained, after which accept ack --readback consumes successfully (the persisted plan keeps planDigest/plannedAt valid for the retry). The error text is correct fail-closed behaviour, not a broken flow; at most the command help omits the intervening resume step, which is documented in orchestration.md and mono-orchestrate.

The rejected ack stays in place, registryEntry.gates stays set, and the attempt's recovery is delayed; the refusal is of legitimate work, since consume-gate-ack.mjs:47-54 deliberately exempts the rejected outcome from exactly these validations.

Breaking input: ack {status:'gates-passed'} carrying only 3 of the 4 dispatched gate names, invoked as `accept ack --outcome rejected`. validatedAck enforces gate coverage unconditionally (accept.mjs:28-30) and then requires passed||blocked (line 34) regardless of the requested outcome, so the request throws before consumeAck is reached. consume-gate-ack.mjs guards the same checks with `outcome !== "rejected"` (lines 47, 49, 54) precisely so invalid gate evidence can be journaled as rejected; recovery of an already journaled rejection hits the same wall because prior.outcome comparison happens after those throws. A direct consume-gate-ack.mjs call remains as a workaround, which bounds the weight.

The orchestrator then applies those lifecycle moves through the connector while the gate list is malformed — the state the contract declares makes the ack unusable and requires attempt termination — and only the later consumeAck (consume-gate-ack.mjs:47 'invalid registry gates') detects it, after the mutations exist.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: workers.json entry with gates:[17] and an ack whose single entry has gate:17, status 'pass', nonempty evidence. validatedAck's registry check (accept.mjs:28) lacks the per-element string/trim test that consume-gate-ack.mjs:47 and the watcher's readRegistryGates apply, so the plan is exposed and lifecycle application proceeds before the producer-contract error surfaces. Trigger requires a malformed registry (producer bug or corruption), which is why this is minor rather than ordinary, but the contract requires complete gate-list validation before lifecycle application.

verdicts.dangerReason: gate-bypass: validatedAck (accept.mjs:18-30) never compares the ack's mtime with the attempt log's birthtime, so an ack file created before this attempt's log — e.g. precreated for attempt N by the attempt N-1 worker, which can write the shared mailbox — is accepted and a lifecycle move plan is printed. The orchestrator then applies the Project→Delivery / Issue-started move on gates the current worker never ran, which is exactly what watch-workers.mjs:757-758 (ackBelongsToAttempt) exists to prevent. The tombstone omission in the same function compounds it: with a .applied/.rejected/.blocked marker in either location and no private record, the remaining raw file is still treated as a new ack and replanned, whereas watch-workers.mjs:624-628 suppresses the whole attempt.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: reports/KEY-gate-ack-a2.json written (with the known default gate names) before the a2 log is created; accept ack validates registry correlation, candidate count and the future-date bound only (accept.mjs:20-25) and prints a plan. The contract states delivery requires the ack's mtime at or after the attempt log's birthtime and that a polling transport applies the same rule; the watcher enforces it at watch-workers.mjs:757. The tombstone half of this finding is tracked separately (see F18) because it needs its own check, but both gaps live in this same unvalidated selection path.

verdicts.dangerReason: data: validateReportBarriers (command-state.mjs:64-68) stops at the FIRST adapter call, and confirmQueue checks each write's durable digest immediately before that write's own adapter call (delivery-state.mjs:171-177), so for a queue [valid, conflicting] only the first write is checked. acceptReport then opens a session and prints both expanded writes (accept.mjs:89). The orchestrator applies write #2 through the connector, mutating the Linear record (e.g. an issue-state change or a second comment) under a write ID whose durable result records a different payload digest — an external record change that the barrier was supposed to prevent and that cannot be excluded as harmless without relying on the later confirm refusal.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: a phase report whose queue's second entry reuses a previously journaled write ID with a changed payload. The sentinel adapter throws on write #1's reconcile, so the loop never reaches write #2's prior-digest comparison; acceptReport proceeds to open the session and print every write. Weight is minor because predecessor validation (requirePredecessors, delivery-state.mjs:167) — the only pre-print obligation the contract names — does run in full, and the trigger needs a worker violating the stable-ID rule.

verdicts.dangerReason: readiness: acceptAmend registers pins.v<n> and workers.json pinsVersion inside launch.lock (accept.mjs:169-173) but releases the lock before invoking resume.mjs (line 175), and the generated resume request {root, issue, resumeFile, extraWritable, workerWritableRoots} carries no version that resumeWorker compares with last_amendment. With two overlapping amendments the v1 prompt can be launched while the registry advertises pinsVersion 2, and the v2 resume then refuses the now-live process (launch.mjs:213-216). The attempt is recorded as running under requirements the worker never received, and its next collection request is refused as 'stale pinsVersion' (command-state.mjs admitUnderLock), so a required amendment fact is missing from the running writer.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: two amend invocations for the same stopped attempt whose prepare phases serialize but whose resume subprocesses interleave. Registration is committed under the lock and the resume runs outside it with no version fence, so the running worker's effective dispatch and the registry's pinsVersion can diverge permanently. Minor weight: the orchestrator is normally a single session, so concurrent amends are unlikely, and the state is recoverable by terminating and resuming with the registered resume request.

verdicts.dangerReason: gate-stall: renderDispatch's final guard (dispatch.mjs:28) tests the whole rendered output, including bytes inserted from the approved Issue/PRD/Spec, so a document containing literal template syntax such as {{issue}} or {{ user.name }} raises 'unfilled dispatch placeholders remain' even though every template placeholder was supplied at line 23. Dispatch therefore refuses to launch approved work — including, in this pack, any Issue that quotes the newly pinned {{...}} placeholder names — and the only workaround is altering the owner-approved snapshot.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: any snapshot document containing a {{token}} literal (no inner braces). String.replace does not rescan replacements, so substitution succeeds, but the post-render regex at dispatch.mjs:28 matches the inserted literal and throws. The guard must be evaluated on the template/unsubstituted regions, not on rendered document content.

verdicts.dangerReason: silent-result: coverage() captures [^\n.]+ after 'Покрывает' (snapshot.mjs:55), so a period inside the text — 'Покрывает R1 (API v1.0), R2.' or a Russian abbreviation such as 'п. 3' — truncates the fragment and R2 is never queued for transitive selection. Requirement definitions are not among the always-included common sections (snapshot.mjs:60-63), so the command reports success and writes prd-extract.md without a requirement the selected unit explicitly covers; the worker receives a silently incomplete snapshot with no refusal or warning.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: a selected definition whose coverage line embeds a period before the last identifier. references() then sees only the prefix, so transitive closure silently omits the trailing IDs; unknown-ID refusal cannot help because the dropped ID is never looked up. Minor weight: real fixtures place the period only at the end of the coverage clause, so the trigger is an unusual but legitimate line shape.

verdicts.dangerReason: gate-stall: scan() stores only the fence character (snapshot.mjs:21), so a line of three backticks inside a four-backtick fence closes the outer block, contrary to CommonMark's same-or-longer closing rule. Example headings inside that block then count as document structure, and section() throws 'missing or duplicate section' (snapshot.mjs:35) for a duplicated 'Кратко'. Dispatch refuses an otherwise valid short-profile Issue whose Spec merely illustrates markdown, and the only workaround is editing the approved document.
verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: a Tech Spec with a four-backtick fence containing a triple-backtick example and a '## Кратко' heading. The inner delimiter matches the stored character and toggles the fence closed, exposing example structure; the duplicate always-included heading makes section() throw and the dispatch refuse. Minor weight because nested-fence examples are uncommon in these documents.

verdicts.dangerReason: Not dangerous on a concrete path: every exact fact the audience matrix insists is carried in full to both columns is present in the rendered prompt — resolved identity command with all four pins, byte-frozen paths and hashes, the complete writable-root list, the gate list, lifecycle moves, mailbox/fallback paths and the verbatim verification lines (templates/orchestrator-dispatch.md:20-50,124-137,165-168). verdicts.reason: Confirmed. prepareDispatch never reads orchestration.workerAudience (it is a validated config key, project-config.mjs:281-286) and renderDispatch strips the generator block (dispatch.mjs:21) without implementing its matrix, so the gpt-worker default and claude-5 produce byte-identical bodies: no explicit parked-reason decision list, no inlined comment/certificate/report shapes, no re-enumerated per-step ordering. The leftover instruction 'Generate profile-required redundancy from that source verbatim' (template line 175) now addresses the worker instead of a generator. This contradicts the contract's audience-adapter section, whose default is described as the safe direction.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed; same mechanism and fix as F1 (reject executable filters, or run the start-gate filter inspection, before creating the worktree). Breaking input identical: filter configured in the product repo, matching .gitattributes in origin/main, worktree absent.

Breaking input: default configuration with no reviewDataset, worker copying the dispatched Preflight pins verbatim into its gate request (exactly as the new test's request builder spreads pins). gate.mjs's absence branch keys on undefined only. Minor weight because a worker that omits the key instead of copying null passes, so the stall depends on how the pins are copied; the emitted representation is still incompatible with the gate it is meant to feed.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Breaking input: issue-only.json with object-valued config and ownerApproval.
