findings.title: Resume the exited worker before consuming its ack
findings.trigger: Use dispatch's default handshake=resume, let the worker exit after its passed ack, then submit fresh plan-bound read-backs to accept ack.
findings.evidence: acceptAck calls consumeAck without preparing or invoking resume.mjs. consumeAck requires last_resume to identify a registered resumed writer and otherwise throws 'resumed writer registration for this ack required before consumption'. The documented command sequence therefore leaves lifecycle moves applied but the worker exited. The fixture bypasses this missing step by manually inserting last_resume into workers.json.

findings.title: Allow terminal rejection of unusable acks
findings.trigger: Call accept ack --outcome rejected for an incomplete passed ack, foreign gate name, or malformed registry gate list.
findings.evidence: validatedAck requires valid coverage and either passed or blocked before considering rejected. Consequently the acks that require terminal rejection cannot reach consumeAck's rejection branch. Recovery also fails for a trusted rejected record containing that original unusable ack. The underlying consumer deliberately exempts rejected outcomes from these coverage requirements.

findings.title: Check that the ack belongs to the current attempt
findings.trigger: A correctly shaped aN ack already exists before the current aN log is created, and the orchestrator polls accept ack.
findings.evidence: The wrapper checks only that ack mtime is not in the future; it never requires mtime >= current log birthtime. The ack contains no attempt field, so matching its filename and registry log basename cannot establish authorship. This stale artifact produces a lifecycle plan even though the watcher correctly excludes it through ackBelongsToAttempt.

findings.title: Honor attempt-wide ack tombstones before planning
findings.trigger: An unconsumed candidate and an .applied, .blocked, or .rejected tombstone exist across the two locations, with no trusted private consumption record.
findings.evidence: Candidate discovery examines only the unsuffixed filenames. Neither validatedAck nor the delegated consumer checks tombstones before treating the remaining candidate as a new signal. accept ack can therefore print a lifecycle plan where the contract and watcher require no ack at all. A tombstone must suppress delivery without authorizing registry cleanup.

findings.title: Validate gate-name types before exposing moves
findings.trigger: The current registry has gates=[""] and the ack reports that same empty name as pass with nonempty evidence.
findings.evidence: validatedAck checks array length and uniqueness but never requires registry gate names to be nonempty strings. This input satisfies passed and exposes a move plan. Only subsequent consumeAck validation rejects the list, after the connector may already have applied lifecycle moves. The contract requires complete registry-list validation before planning.

findings.title: Preserve the validated ack binding through consumption
findings.trigger: In wait mode, the worker-writable ack is replaced between read-back validation and consumeAck acquiring launch.lock.
findings.evidence: The validation transaction returns only outcome and readback, releases its lock, and calls consumeAck, which resolves the locations and reads the ack again. No expected path or ackDigest survives this boundary. Consumption can consequently publish a record for different ack bytes than the printed plan validated; the waiting worker then rejects that record against its own digest.

findings.title: Validate every write before printing connector instructions
findings.trigger: A valid later-sequence report queues two writes, and the second reuses an earlier write ID with a changed payload.
findings.evidence: The sentinel adapter throws at the first write, so confirmQueue never reaches the second write's durable writeDigest comparison. acceptReport then opens a session and prints both writes. Confirmation eventually rejects the conflicting second ID, but only after its changed payload may have been applied through the connector. The entire queue must be checked before exposing writes.

findings.title: Reject executable Git filters before creating the worktree
findings.trigger: The repository config defines a smudge/process filter used by a tracked file, and the Issue worktree does not exist.
findings.evidence: git worktree add checks out tracked files and can execute configured filters in the orchestrator process environment. The local git wrapper disables hooks and fsmonitor but does not inspect filters. startGate's rejectExecutableFilters runs only afterward, so its refusal occurs after repository-configured code has already executed outside the worker sandbox.

findings.title: Emit the established project-first context seam
findings.trigger: Dispatch any project-first Issue without issue-only.json.
findings.evidence: The generated seam sets risk_class to the delivery risk and approval_status to approved, pending, or rejected. The existing resolver and references/issue-only-lane.md require risk_class=null and approval_status=absent for project-first. Every such dispatch therefore supplies facts outside the seam's domain to the worker's mandatory context check; package approval belongs in its separate approval record.

findings.title: Serialize structured issue-only facts into the prompt
findings.trigger: issue-only.json supplies config and ownerApproval as JSON objects containing the owner principal and authenticated approval fingerprint.
findings.evidence: These accepted values are passed directly to renderDispatch, which renders them using String(value). Both become '[object Object]', losing the owner, configuration and approval facts needed by the snapshot-only worker. context_seam is explicitly JSON-stringified, but the accompanying authentication facts are not.

findings.title: Allow literal template syntax inside snapshot bodies
findings.trigger: An approved Issue or full document contains a literal such as {{user.name}}, for example when implementing a Handlebars template.
findings.evidence: Template substitution inserts snapshot bodies verbatim, then the final regex scans the entire rendered result for double-brace expressions. It rejects legitimate document content as an unfilled dispatch placeholder. All source-template placeholders were already checked by the replacement callback, so inserted data must not be interpreted again.

findings.title: Apply the configured worker audience during generation
findings.trigger: Generate dispatches with workerAudience=gpt-worker or workerAudience=claude-5.
findings.evidence: prepareDispatch never reads workerAudience, and renderDispatch varies only the optional pilot block. It removes the generator instructions while leaving 'Generate profile-required redundancy' in the worker prompt. Thus the default gpt-worker dispatch lacks the mandated inline output skeletons and explicit parked-reason decision list, and neither audience receives its configured adaptation. This work belongs to the generator, not the dispatched worker.

findings.title: Track fence length when excluding code examples
findings.trigger: A document uses a four-backtick fenced Markdown example containing ordinary three-backtick fences and a sample '- R99. Example' line.
findings.evidence: scan stores only the delimiter character, so the inner three-backtick line incorrectly closes the four-backtick fence. The sample R99 becomes a real indexed definition, allowing coverage of an otherwise nonexistent ID to dispatch example text instead of refusing. Closing fences must match the opening character and meet its length.

findings.title: Reject executable filters before checking out the worktree
findings.trigger: Dispatch a new worktree from a repository whose Git configuration defines a smudge/process filter selected by a tracked .gitattributes file.
findings.evidence: The command runs `git worktree add` before invoking gate.mjs. Its Git wrapper disables hooks and fsmonitor but does not reject executable filters, so checkout executes the configured filter in the orchestrator process environment. The existing gate.mjs filter rejection happens afterward and cannot undo that execution.

findings.title: Reconcile an already resumed attempt before printing another move plan
findings.trigger: The orchestrator crashes after registering a resumed writer but before publishing the consumption record; the passed ack remains, possibly beside the worker's report.
findings.evidence: With no private record, acceptAck unconditionally publishes a fresh lifecycle plan. Neither validatedAck nor the plan branch inspects last_resume or the adjacent stage report. This presents already-applied lifecycle moves as a new application plan in the exact crash window that the handshake contract requires reconciling before replay.

findings.title: Register the resumed writer on the default handshake path
findings.trigger: A default handshake=resume worker exits after its passed ack, and the orchestrator supplies the printed plan's fresh read-backs to accept ack.
findings.evidence: acceptAck immediately calls consumeAck without preparing or invoking resume.mjs. consumeAck requires a matching last_resume registration before applied consumption, so the documented flow stops with `resumed writer registration for this ack required before consumption`. Only acceptAmend invokes resume.mjs; the command fixture masks this gap by manually inserting last_resume.

findings.title: Allow invalid gate coverage to reach rejected consumption
findings.trigger: An ack omits a required gate, contains a foreign gate, or has malformed registry gates, and the orchestrator invokes accept ack --outcome rejected.
findings.evidence: validatedAck rejects invalid coverage before considering rejection, and its outcome condition requires either a valid passed ack or a valid blocked ack even for outcome=rejected. Consequently the wrapper cannot journal and consume the malformed acknowledgements that rejection exists to handle. Recovery of a rejected record containing the same invalid ack also fails before cleanup.

findings.title: Apply attempt freshness and tombstone rules before exposing moves
findings.trigger: The sole unconsumed ack predates the current attempt log, or an unconsumed mailbox ack coexists with an attempt tombstone in the fallback location.
findings.evidence: Candidate validation checks only unconsumed-file count and future mtime. It never compares ack mtime with log birthtime or checks .applied/.rejected/.blocked markers in either location. Such artifacts therefore produce lifecycle plans although watch-workers.mjs deliberately rejects them as non-authoritative for this attempt.

findings.title: Validate every durable gate name before publishing a plan
findings.trigger: registryEntry.gates is a nonempty unique array containing an empty string or non-string, and a passed ack repeats those values.
findings.evidence: The wrapper checks array length and uniqueness but never requires nonempty string gate names. For example, gates=[""] with a matching pass entry reaches plan publication. consumeAck later rejects the same registry shape, after the orchestrator has already received and potentially applied the lifecycle instructions.

findings.title: Bind consumption to the ack validated against the plan
findings.trigger: The worker-writable ack changes after read-back validation releases launch.lock and before consumeAck acquires that lock.
findings.evidence: The validated action carries only outcome and readback, discarding the validated ackDigest and artifact identity. consumeAck rereads the candidate and can consume a different shape-valid ack using read-backs authorized against the original plan. This breaks the exact-artifact binding and can publish a consumption digest that the waiting worker rejects.

findings.title: Finish startup consumption recovery before accepting phase reports
findings.trigger: A resumed worker publishes a phase report while its startup ack and registry gates remain because consumption was interrupted.
findings.evidence: acceptReport checks phase correlation and phase predecessors, then opens a session and can confirm the queue. None of correlatedPhase, validateReportBarriers, or admitUnderLock reconciles the startup ack/private record or retained gates. An empty queue is even confirmed inside validateReportBarriers. The worker can therefore advance while the unresolved startup ack continues suppressing execution liveness.

findings.title: Check conflicts across the entire queue before printing writes
findings.trigger: A report contains a new first write followed by a write ID previously used in the attempt with a different payload.
findings.evidence: confirmQueue checks each durable writeDigest immediately before that write's adapter call. The sentinel adapter throws on the first item, so validation never reaches later conflicts. acceptReport then prints all connector instructions; the changed later write is rejected only during final confirmation, after its external mutation may already have occurred.

findings.title: Keep ordinary report acceptance available for legacy unpinned launches
findings.trigger: A permitted legacy full/resume registry entry omits pins and publishes a normal comment or empty phase queue.
findings.evidence: acceptReport always calls admitUnderLock, which unconditionally calls effectivePins before checking whether the queue contains a collection. effectivePins throws when entry.pins is absent. Thus even ordinary connector queues from supported legacy launches cannot use the new acceptance path; an empty queue may already have been confirmed before the command fails.

findings.title: Reject in-place risk escalation outside the issue-only envelope
findings.trigger: An approved issue-only attempt is amended from standard to deep or risky.
findings.evidence: The risk validation permits the escalation, and the full-snapshot requirement explicitly exempts packageKind=issue-only. The command then registers the new pins and resumes the same delivery. The existing issue-only contract permits only tiny/standard and requires parking and restarting Project-first when risk leaves that envelope.

findings.title: Preserve the existing Project-first seam values
findings.trigger: Dispatch any Project-first package without issue-only.json.
findings.evidence: The generated seam sets risk_class to the delivery risk and approval_status to approved/pending/rejected. The fixed five-field contract in references/issue-only-lane.md and projectFirstResult in resolve-issue-context.mjs instead require risk_class=null and approval_status=absent for Project-first. Every such dispatch supplies contradictory machine facts to mono-implement's seam-resolution gate.

findings.title: Track fence length when excluding example definitions
findings.trigger: A PRD contains a four-backtick fenced Markdown example with an inner triple-backtick line and an example `- R99. ...`; the Issue references R99, which has no real definition.
findings.evidence: scan stores only the fence character and closes a fence on any same-character delimiter. The inner triple-backtick line therefore closes the outer four-backtick fence, exposing the example R99 as a real definition. extractSnapshot accepts the nonexistent requirement instead of refusing the unknown key.

findings.trigger: A legacy attempt leaves an uncaptured, orphaned process running `make -C/absolute/worktree serve` in a separate process group.

findings.title: Distinguish environment markers from command arguments
findings.trigger: On macOS, an unrelated process outside the control invocation runs a command such as `rg --fixed-strings MONO_ATTEMPT=<previous-marker> some-file`, without that environment variable.
findings.evidence: The `ps eww` command column contains argv together with environment text. Splitting the entire column and searching for the marker treats the literal argv token as an inherited environment marker. requireProcessOwnership then reports the unrelated PID as a remnant and refuses both stopped-tree reconciliation and backup launch.

findings.title: Handle full process output beyond the default buffer
findings.trigger: The host's aggregate full command lines exceed 1 MiB, for example with several concurrent Codex processes carrying large dispatch prompts in argv.
findings.evidence: The new `ps -ww` invocation requests unlimited-width commands but leaves execFileSync's default 1 MiB maxBuffer unchanged. Exceeding it throws ENOBUFS before processTable returns. findings.title: Do not treat a locale change as proof of PID reuse
findings.trigger: A legacy attempt captured a detached process-group leader under a localized locale. During backup reconciliation under LC_ALL=C, that same process remains alive with a neutral command and no attempt marker.
findings.evidence: processStart and processTable deliberately preserve caller-localized start strings. groupReused treats any string difference as PID reuse, so capturedLive ignores the still-live captured group and both group-probe loops skip it. reachesCapture also compares the raw strings. With no marker or path reference, stop reconciliation and validateBackupLaunch therefore accept a surviving captured process. Verify actual incarnation changes without interpreting locale differences as reuse.

findings.title: Check the previous collector before excluding caller descendants
findings.trigger: A persistent controller starts the worker and collector through the exported APIs, then stops/retires the worker and requests its backup while the old collector or gate remains alive.
findings.evidence: collectorStart creates a child of the controller. requireProcessOwnership adds every controller descendant to controls and skips those rows before checking the matching collector lock, its gate, ancestry or marker. The earlier survivor checks cover the worker capture, which excludes the separately launched collector. Consequently validateBackupLaunch can admit a backup alongside the old collector and its active verification work. Attempt-owned collectors must take precedence over the control-process exclusion.

findings.title: Handle command-table output beyond the default buffer limit

findings.trigger: Host process command lines collectively exceed 1 MiB, for example with several concurrent Codex workers carrying large prompts in argv.

findings.title: Avoid the default buffer limit for full process commands

findings.title: Recognize phase reports and confirmations as attempt artifacts
findings.trigger: A legacy attempt leaves an uncaptured orphan in a separate group whose command references only its mailbox phase report and attempt-numbered confirmation, such as delivery-state.mjs wait --report /control/reports/MONO-7-phase-code.json --confirmation /control/confirmations/MONO-7-phase-code-a1-s1.confirmed.json.

With no captured ancestry/group and no legacy marker, otherSignal is false and marker is absent, so both stopped-tree reconciliation and backup launch accept the surviving command. findings.title: Retain collector gate identities after their locks are cleaned up
findings.trigger: A collection gate leaves a background descendant in its dedicated process group with closed stdio, then exits; the collector subsequently stops normally before the backup switch.
findings.evidence: Ownership detection obtains collector and gate groups only from the current collector lock. However, collector.mjs runGate deletes holder.gate after the gate process closes, and withLock removes the collector lock when the collector exits. Neither group is retained in the worker attempt's processes or retirement record. A surviving descendant with a neutral command has no worker MONO_ATTEMPT because the collector launches outside the worker transport. Consequently, requireProcessOwnership ignores it and permits switching despite the previously registered gate group's surviving descendant, which may still access the shared worktree.

findings.title: Recognize paths attached to directory options
findings.trigger: A legacy attempt leaves an orphaned process in an uncaptured group running `make -C/absolute/worktree watch`, where `/absolute/worktree` is the attempt's worktree.
findings.evidence: The character immediately before the worktree reference is `C`, which the boundary expression rejects. With no retained ancestry/group and no marker on a legacy attempt, requireProcessOwnership therefore ignores this live process during both stopped-tree reconciliation and backup launch. The backup can start while the old build continues modifying the same checkout. Attached directory options are valid path references and need recognition.
